title: Hazel and the Spire
premise: When the border wards of Thornfell collapse on the night the stars vanish, beast-speaker and smuggler Xanthe Vane discovers the wards were fed by dragon-fire — and the last dragon, imprisoned beneath the Spire for a century, is dying. Hunted by the Wardens who once sheltered her, Xanthe must smuggle the dragon's stolen heart-flame across the mountains with a disgraced Warden captain, Corin Ashe, whose duty demands he arrest her. As they fall in love and gather a ragtag found family of outcasts, Xanthe must choose between returning the flame to free the dragon (reigniting the ancient war) or letting it gutter out (dooming all magic). She finds a third path: binding the flame into the found family itself, so the fire lives in many hearts instead of one captive beast — ending the war before it begins, at the cost of her own gift.
about_author: Tamsin Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former wildlife rehabilitator who spent a decade listening to things that cannot speak. She writes fantasy about creatures on the edge of extinction from a crooked farmhouse in the northern hills.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Smuggling moon-wool through Thornfell passes, she hears the mountain animals fall silent as every star vanishes overhead. The border wards collapse like cut harp strings. Emotional beat: dread and wonder colliding; her secret gift nearly exposed when a dying fox begs her for help.

chapters.title: What the Fox Knew
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Sheltering in a waystation, she questions the wounded fox, which speaks of 'the caged fire going dark' beneath the Spire. Wardens arrive searching for a beast-speaker. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into resolve; she chooses to run toward the Spire rather than away.

chapters.title: The Captain Without a Badge
chapters.summary: Corin's POV. Disgraced Warden captain Corin Ashe is ordered to hunt the beast-speaker blamed for the ward-fall. He recognizes the description — the woman who once saved his life. Emotional beat: duty warring with gratitude; he accepts the commission to control the hunt himself.

chapters.title: Smoke on the Pass
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Ambushed by Wardens at Greytooth Pass, Xanthe is saved by an unlikely trio: Brack the trollish stonemason, Pip the pickpocket child, and Marisol, a hedge-witch. Emotional beat: reluctant trust; the first stitches of a found family sewn under fire.

chapters.title: The Spire's Shadow
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Xanthe reaches the Spire city and witnesses the Wardens' cover-up: refugees blamed, curfews, propaganda. Corin arrives undercover, hunting her. Emotional beat: outrage and grief; Xanthe realizes the corruption runs deeper than one fallen ward.

chapters.title: A Bargain in Ash
chapters.summary: Corin's POV. Corin corners Xanthe in a burned granary but hesitates; she shows him the dying fox and the truth of the heart-flame. He lets her go — treason. Emotional beat: guilt and awakening; his faith in the Wardens cracks.

chapters.title: Down Beneath the Roots
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Guided by rats and roots, the group infiltrates the Spire's undercrofts and finds the last dragon, Ysolde, ancient and fading, her heart-flame half-stolen by the High Warden. Emotional beat: awe and heartbreak; Xanthe promises the dragon freedom.

chapters.title: Theft of Fire
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. The crew steals the vial of heart-flame from the Warden vaults, but Pip is captured. Emotional beat: terror and sacrifice; Marisol burns her own magic reserves to buy their escape, revealing how much power costs.

chapters.title: Interrogation
chapters.summary: Pip's POV. In a Warden cell, Pip endures questioning by the charming, chilling High Warden Sarel Voss, who offers the child comfort and lies. Emotional beat: loneliness met with stubborn courage; Pip gives nothing away but learns Voss wants war.

chapters.title: The Long Road North
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Fleeing north with the flame, the group bonds around a campfire — stories, griefs, Pip's rescue negotiated by Corin's old contacts. Emotional beat: warmth against cold; the found family solidifies, and Xanthe and Corin admit what they feel.

chapters.title: Voss Descends
chapters.summary: Sarel's POV. The High Warden reveals her design: let the dragon die, harvest the flame as a weapon, blame the beast-speakers, and unify the realm through holy war. Emotional beat: cold ambition; readers see the corruption of power wearing a righteous face.

chapters.title: The Traitor's Choice
chapters.summary: Corin's POV. A former brother-in-arms offers Corin reinstatement if he delivers Xanthe. He refuses and sends warning instead, burning his last bridge. Emotional beat: love over duty made explicit; Corin becomes a fugitive too.

chapters.title: Where Dragons Once Slept
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. The group reaches the ruined Dragonfast crater, where the flame could be returned — but returning it would arm Ysolde for vengeance and reignite the ancient war. Emotional beat: moral vertigo; every path leads through fire.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Crater Rim
chapters.summary: Brack's POV. Voss's elite Wardens attack. Brack holds the pass alone so the others can escape, gravely wounded. Emotional beat: quiet heroism; the gentle giant bleeds for people who were strangers a month ago.

chapters.title: The Guttering
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. The heart-flame begins to fail — it can only live in a willing vessel. Xanthe takes it into herself, gaining terrible power and a countdown. Emotional beat: sacrifice and intoxication; she feels the pull of the flame's rage.

chapters.title: What Power Whispers
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. The flame tempts Xanthe with visions of vengeance; she nearly kills a captured Warden scout before Corin reaches her. Emotional beat: horror at herself; she understands how dragons fell, how Voss was made.

chapters.title: The Siege of Havenhollow
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Voss's forces corner the family in the free-town of Havenhollow; townsfolk shelter them, and Marisol rallies hedge-witches to hold the walls. Emotional beat: solidarity; ordinary people choosing each other over empire.

chapters.title: The Last Dragon Rises
chapters.summary: Ysolde's POV (a first — rendered through Xanthe's link). Freed by the flame's departure, the dying dragon rises from the Spire and comes not to burn but to witness. Emotional beat: majesty and sorrow; the ancient war pauses on one outstretched wing.

chapters.title: Fire Against Fire
chapters.summary: Climax, Xanthe's POV. Confrontation atop the Spire: Xanthe, carrying the flame, faces Voss, who has bound stolen magic into herself. Corin and the family fight through the Wardens below. Emotional beat: fury and clarity; Xanthe refuses both vengeance and surrender.

chapters.title: The Third Path
chapters.summary: Climax resolved, Xanthe's POV. Instead of freeing the flame into one body or letting it die, Xanthe splits it — binding shards into her chosen family, each willingly given and received. Voss, unable to seize a fire spread across many hearts, falls. Emotional beat: transcendence through shared burden; power dispersed defeats power hoarded.

chapters.title: Ashes and Acorns
chapters.summary: Corin's POV. Aftermath: the Wardens reform under new oaths, Ysolde becomes guardian rather than weapon, and the family plants a hearth-tree where the Spire's dungeons stood. Xanthe's gift is fading with the flame she gave away. Emotional beat: bittersweet peace; love outlasting magic.

chapters.title: Every Heart a Hearth
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Xanthe's POV. One year later, Xanthe can no longer speak with beasts — but the fox visits anyway, and Pip swears she still understands. The stars return. Emotional beat: quiet joy; what was lost in magic was gained in belonging, and the fire keeps them all warm.
